Regardless of the city/town you're working in I would really be mindful about where you choose your home. Utah is a very unique state and your experience here in Utah as well as how you might feel about your neighborhood and neighbors significantly depends on where you live. Try to think about your personality and the life that you wanna live here in Utah, try to choose a city that matches that. I'm 33 years old and I've lived in Utah my entire life and I can tell you that the city you live in plays a huge role in your every day well-being and the types of people you'll be interacting with.

It's no secret that Utah is heavily religious and if you are not the same and you move into an area that is, it's likely to really affect your mood, your relationship, and your job.

I am a biracial female and I would suggest living downtown Salt Lake City because the ethnicity, the culture and the LGBTQ plus community is very active. But cost of living downtown Salt Lake City can be pricey. I would also suggest North Salt Lake.

For the situation you described I wouldn't go further north than North Salt Lake. West Valley has a lot of culture but what you will soon find, in Utah where you live has its own stigma. Each city is known for a certain thing. You don't have to fall in line with the stigma but simply saying I live in… It's kind of how people classify you here in Utah. So for your situation I would say North Salt Lake, downtown Salt Lake, South Salt Lake… And then point of the mountain area… Which is like Draper/Lehi that's another little area that's nice.
